steps.content: You're in a hair salon bathed in sunshine coming through the giant French windows. You're there with Adela. Ever since the Dorset Street investigation, her power has been kept in check with the help of the shackles. As a result, the number of attacks has decreased dramatically. But you know that that's not the end.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: So this is your surprise for me?

You told me that you had stayed in the MBCC headquarters for too long and you were starting to feel claustrophobic. I figured that spending some time away from that place might make you feel a bit better. So, here we are.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Thank you, for doing this for me. I appreciate it.
The hair salon is located in a bustling pedestrian zone of Eastside, but for some inexplicable reason, there are no customers in the shop.
Adela doesn't seem deflated. She continues to wipe down the already-spotless table.

options: Sorry, I should've done some promotions.

choices.text: Sorry, I should've done some promotions.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: It's okay.
You feel a bit awkward, but quickly relax when you see a woman coming in. You come up to her.
Welcome. New shop, twenty percent off for all customers.
She is middle-aged, with slightly disheveled hair. Lines have found their way onto her face, but it's not hard to see that she must have been a beauty in her younger days.
She looks at you in confusion, her hand holding a coupon for a free haircut.
She's the person you've been waiting for.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Welcome. Please come in and have a seat.
You turn around and glance at Adela. She looks calm, but you're sure that she recognizes the woman. It's her mother; it's impossible that she doesn't remember what her mother looks like.

steps.speaker: Kelly
steps.content: Oh, okay.
Adela comes near you and gives you a meaningful look. You shrug, and after a long second, she sighs with resignation.

steps.speaker: Kelly
steps.content: I've lucked out. See? A coupon for a free haircut.
Adela has left to get her tools ready. Kelly leans sideways and whispers to you. There's a playfulness about her demeanor that belies her nearly-fifty years.

steps.speaker: Kelly
steps.content: She's a good girl, I can tell. Very warm and friendly.

steps.speaker: Kelly
steps.content: Lucky you. Landed a beautiful and competent girl like that.
You wave your hand in embarrassment. You're about to set Kelly straight about the relationship between you and Adela when she returns with her tool kit.
Not saying a word, Adela removes a pair of scissors from the tool kit and starts trimming Kelly's hair.
Normally, Kelly, who has little tolerance for disrespectful behavior, would complain aloud about the hairdresser cutting her hair without asking her first.

But it feels different today. As she looks at the hairdresser's reflection in the mirror and feels her gentle fingers weaving in and out of her hair, she's overwhelmed with an inexplicable feeling of familiarity and security.
A while later, as if to break the silence, Kelly speaks to Adela.

steps.speaker: Kelly
steps.content: You know what? I used to know a girl who also wanted to become a hairdresser.
There's a slight pause in Adela's moving hands. She looks up at the woman's reflection, and nods with a smile on her face to show that she's listening, trimming the woman's hair all the while.

steps.speaker: Kelly
steps.content: I didn't understand back then what's so good about being a hairdresser.

steps.speaker: Kelly
steps.content: Now I do. A good haircut can put you in a good mood. A good hairdresser makes all the difference. I misunderstood the girl.

steps.speaker: Kelly
steps.content: Not really. It's just that the kids in the nursery are a headache for me.

steps.speaker: Kelly
steps.content: I wash their diapers, I get up before it's light, day in, day out. They run around all day like a bunch of monkeys. They're really doing my head in.

steps.speaker: Kelly
steps.content: You might not believe this, but I used to be a ballerina working for a big ballet company in Eastside. The world was my oyster back then. Even after I left the company, there was no lack of attention from men. Now, look at me, slaving away in a nursery.

steps.speaker: Kelly
steps.content: I don't know what I was thinking when I took that job. Those little Misters and Misses, they're the bane of my life.
Despite her continual complaints, it doesn't seem to you that she hates her job that much, judging by the expression on her face.
Adela is working away on Kelly's hair. Bits of hair are drifting onto the floor.

options: Have you heard about Mad Shears?

choices.text: Have you heard about Mad Shears?

steps.content: Your question takes Kelly by surprise. Confused, she answers your question.

steps.speaker: Kelly
steps.content: Mad Shears? Who's that?
Adela is also surprised by your question. The muscles of her hand holding the scissors tense, and her work slows down a bit.
For some reason, you're amused by Adela's reaction. And then you go on to explain the story of Mad Shears to Kelly.
It's a famous urban myth going around in Eastside. It's rumored that this Mad Shears can trim away other people's worries by removing the memories they don't want to face.
You can seek her out. Maybe she'll help you get rid of the worries you're having because of your job.
Kelly pauses for a moment and gives an embarrassed smile.

steps.speaker: Kelly
steps.content: I don't think that's for me...

steps.speaker: Kelly
steps.content: Those little monkeys give me hell, but I love them. That was just a bit of a complaint, that's all.

steps.speaker: Kelly
steps.content: Sometimes, I feel like, um, I had a kid once. It's a very strange feeling.

steps.speaker: Kelly
steps.content: I'd have made a terrible mother. I don't deserve to have a kid.
Kelly sounds despondent. And Adela has just finished her job.

The general shape of Kelly's hair hasn't changed much. All Adela did was cut off some split ends and make some small adjustments here and there. But the effect is obvious. She now looks a few years younger than before she had the haircut, and much more pleasing to the eye.
Kelly looks at her reflection and fingers her hair. For some reason, tears well in her eyes.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Are you not happy with the haircut?

steps.speaker: Kelly
steps.content: No, it's not that. I love the haircut. It suits me.

steps.speaker: Kelly
steps.content: The girl I mentioned earlier, she used to cut my hair in this style. It was years ago, and I've never changed my hairstyle since then. I have the feeling I knew her very well, but I just can't remember her name. It's very strange.
Her voice breaks. Realizing that she might have made a faux pas, she starts apologizing.

steps.speaker: Kelly
steps.content: Sorry, forgive me for talking nonsense. It seems to be a side effect of getting old, talking nonsense.
Kelly wipes the tears from the corners of her eyes. And self-consciously, she adds:

steps.speaker: Kelly
steps.content: I've been told that I have a tendency to ramble. I've been working on it, and I've been doing a decent job.

steps.speaker: Kelly
steps.content: I don't know what's wrong with me today. I can't seem to shut up around you.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Don't worry about it. I'm glad that you shared your story with us.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: After all, it's part of my job as a hairdresser to listen to my customers' troubles.

steps.speaker: Kelly
steps.content: Thank you.
Kelly stands up slowly and walks toward the door.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Thank you for your business.
Kelly turns her head to look at Adela.

steps.speaker: Kelly
steps.content: Oh, thank you. You did a great job. I'll come back for your services again.
Adela nods, wearing a warm smile on her face.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Look forward to seeing you again.
Adela's eyes follow Kelly until she's out of sight. Adela then turns around to face you.
You look at her, feeling somewhat guilty.

options: I shouldn't have sprung this on you. Sorry.

choices.text: I shouldn't have sprung this on you. Sorry.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: You have nothing to be sorry for. I should thank you, if anything.
I just did what I could to help.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Despite the fact that you relish interfering in other people's business, enjoy making decisions for them, and use the shackles on them whenever you see fit.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Because of you, I can no longer erase my worries as easily as I did before. Because of you, I have to face the void in my heart and even the past I once left behind.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: I feel exposed because of you, Mr. ${PlayerName}.
steps.female_content: I feel exposed because of you, Miss ${PlayerName}.

steps.content: You don't know how to respond to Adela's accusations.
Sorry...

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Hair grows and grows, until it becomes a heavy burden. I've seen it happen to many, many people, and I've also seen their desire to be free of it. And then you showed up and told me you didn't want to get rid of it, because it's important to you.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: I didn't understand at first. I didn't understand why you didn't want to have your worries erased for your peace of mind, or why you put yourself in harm's way and went to extraordinary lengths to catch me.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: And after you detained me, you delved into my past and forced me to face what's really troubling me.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: I had been running away from my past, and in the process, I had lost something precious.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Fortunately for me, you were always there for me every time I got lost.

options: I looked into your past, and I knew you wanted to stay.

choices.text: I looked into your past, and I knew you wanted to stay.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Ah, before I knew it, my "peaceful" life had been turned upside down, and I didn't get to leave.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: I still have the hairs associated with you, but I don't find them irritating. They feel like a reassuring weight that anchors me.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: I feel that it's okay to keep them this time.
Adela looks at you, her eyes full of gentleness.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: So...

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Mr. Inspector, let me accompany you on the journey ahead, me with all my newly-recovered worrisome memories.
steps.female_content: Miss Inspector, let me accompany you on the journey ahead, me with all my newly-recovered worrisome memories.
